:::{#hero-heading}

I am a Postdoctoral Scholar within [Sagan Friant's RISK lab](https://www.saganfriant.com/) at Pennsylvania State University, primarily working on the [SCAPES](lassa/SCAPES.qmd) project. I am also a Fellow-in-Residence with the [Verena Consortium](https://www.viralemergence.org/) working with [Stephanie Seifert](https://labs.wsu.edu/mezap/) on a study investigating the ecological and molecular drivers of [cross-species transmission of arenaviruses and hantaviruses](arha.qmd). 

Starting in September 2026, I will take up an independent research role as a Birgitta Sintring Fellow at the [Department of Ecology and Genetics, Uppsala University](https://www.uu.se/en/department/ecology-and-genetics). My project will focus on developing a microbial sensor to investigate indirect contact networks among bank voles, aiming to better understand the transmission dynamics of rodent-borne viruses.

I completed my PhD at the University of London in early 2024. My doctoral research was based across the [Centre for Emerging, Endemic and Exotic diseases](https://www.rvc.ac.uk/research/research-centres-and-facilities/ceeed) (CEEED) at the Royal Veterinary College, the [Centre for Biodiversity and Environment Research](https://www.ucl.ac.uk/biosciences/gee/ucl-centre-biodiversity-and-environment-research) (CBER) at University College London, and the [Department of Clinical Research](https://www.lshtm.ac.uk/research/faculties/itd/crd) at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, funded through a [BBSRC](https://bbsrc.ukri.org/) PhD studentship with the [LIDo DTP](https://www.lido-dtp.ac.uk/).

My research interests fit within the fields of [Planetary Health](https://unfccc.int/climate-action/momentum-for-change/planetary-health) and [One Health](https://www.cdc.gov/onehealth/basics/index.html), with a particular focus on how anthropogenic change affects the risk of zoonotic disease emergence. I use whole-systems approaches to understand the interaction between human and biological factors on these risks. I currently live in Stockholm, Sweden.

:::

## Doctoral Research

My PhD research was mainly carried out in Sierra Leone, West Africa, using [Lassa fever](lassa.qmd), [Monkeypox](monkeypox.qmd), and [Ebola](https://www.cdc.gov/vhf/ebola/) as model disease systems. I adopt interdisciplinary approaches using methods from clinical medicine, epidemiology, mathematical modelling, and systems biology. I am a member of the [PANDORA-ID-net](https://pandora.tghn.org/) consortium and work closely with collaborators on the [One Health theme](https://pandora.tghn.org/one-health/). My fieldwork is conducted with colleagues based at Njala University in Sierra Leone. With this work, I aim to develop dynamic models of disease risk and translate these into policy implementations to promote the health and wellbeing of human communities in low-resource settings.

I am a proponent of Open Science; where possible, pre-specified research questions and study protocols are posted to the [Open Science Framework](https://osf.io/dashboard). I strive to make all code used for my analyses available in reproducible files hosted on my [GitHub](https://github.com/diddrog11) page. All data are hosted on open data repositories (e.g., [GBIF](https://www.gbif.org/), [PHAROS](https://pharos.viralemergence.org/)) and are linked to the projects on this website.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Public Health & Clinical Experience

Prior to leaving the UK, I practiced as a clinician with the [Hospital for Tropical Diseases](http://www.thehtd.org) and in the emergency department at University College London Hospital. My [**CV (PDF)**](cv.pdf) contains a full list of my clinical work.

Alongside my clinical work during the COVID-19 pandemic, I contributed to LSHTM's [Centre for Mathematical Modelling of Infectious Diseases](https://cmmid.github.io/topics/covid19/) to understand the transmission dynamics of SARS-CoV-2. More recently, I worked with the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) in the Outbreak Surveillance Team during the emergence of the Omicron variant, where I developed an automated approach to monitor real-time cases to inform the initial public health response. I was also involved in the UK Monkeypox outbreak, investigating transmission parameters from contact tracing data.

I am currently out of clinical practice while I improve my Swedish language proficiency to transfer my medical qualifications.
